findings.title: The app is right less often than saying up every time
findings.text: 54% of 5,003 graded calls were right. Saying up on every one of them would have been right 57% of the time. So far the forecasts have not shown skill beyond the market's normal upward drift.

findings.title: Down calls are where most of the wrongs come from
findings.text: Calls that said down were right 47% of the time (2,091 calls). Over 10 years a big stock rose over the next 5 days 49% of the time, so a down call starts behind.

findings.title: Hourly calls are worse than a coin flip
findings.text: 46% right on 1,061 hourly calls. Short windows are mostly noise.

findings.title: The model's confidence does not mean much yet
findings.text: When nearly all model runs agreed, calls were right 52%; when it barely agreed, 55%. A higher score has not meant a better call.

findings.title: The record is short
findings.text: All 5,003 graded calls come from 10 trading days (2026-09-28 to 2026-11-19). Calls made on the same day rise and fall together, so this is closer to 10 tests than 5,003.

fixes.rule: Grade against always-up, not against a coin flip
fixes.why: 50% is the wrong bar for stocks, which rise more often than they fall. The report card now shows the always-up number beside the hit rate.

fixes.rule: Stop making down calls on single stocks
fixes.why: In 10 years no simple setup had big stocks falling more often than rising over 5 days. The weakest one (sharp two-day drop while in an uptrend) still rose 3% of the time. A down call fights the drift every time.
They have been right less than half the time. Short windows are mostly noise.

fixes.rule: Lean in when the market is scared, ease off when it is greedy
fixes.why: Stocks rose 7% of the time over the next 5 days when the fear and greed score was under 25, against 49% on a normal day and 4% when it was over 75.

fixes.rule: Wait for more days before trusting the score
fixes.why: The record covers 10 trading days. About 60 is the minimum to tell skill from luck.

bottom_line: With those rules the same log scores 65% on 2,444 calls. Always-up on those calls scores 65%, so the rules remove bad calls but do not create skill. The honest way to more right calls is fewer, better-chosen calls, then waiting for proof.
